title: Canary Lab Sprint Notebook for Graded Exposure
content:
Goal: Quick field notebook for a 2-week sprint to run micro-canaries using a graded exposure pattern (0.1% -> 1% -> 5% traffic) with strong human-in-loop checkpoints and automated thermal controls. This is intentionally pragmatic — minimal ceremony, fast learning cycles, and a clear escape hatch.

Context / why this is different
- We want short, frequent canaries that explicitly measure cost/latency and semantic regressions together. Many canary docs focus solely on functional signal (errors, p99). This notebook pairs quality probes with unit-economics probes for the same slices.
- Graded exposure: each stage introduces more traffic but narrows the observation window to a handful of high-value slices (search, checkout messages, reranker calls).

Sprint plan (2 weeks)
- Day 0: kickoff, steward and observer assignment, smoke fixtures deployed to canary group.
- Days 1-2: Stage A (0.1%): warm caches, collect baseline latencies, token counts, and quality probes.
- Days 3-4: Pause + human review session (30 min). Decision: advance / hold / revert.
- Days 5-6: Stage B (1%): broaden slices, enable KV cache telemetry, OOM watch.
- Day 7: Automated safety window evaluation + steward sign-off.
- Days 8-10: Stage C (5%): stress on routing and fallback policies.
- Day 11: Cohort-level A/B comparisons, small offline evals against golden prompts.
- Day 12: Roll to ramp or revert; write short postmortem.

Key roles and brief responsibilities
- Steward (primary): runs the activation timeline, makes go/hold/revert decision after observing signals.
- Observer (telemetry): validates metric ingestion, sanity-checks signal deltas, runs quick SQL slices.
- Quality lead (ML): inspects hallucination markers, runs a batch of golden prompts.
- Ops (SRE): watches infra, enforces circuit breakers, owns the reversion automation.
- Comms (PM): prepares user-facing notes and coordinates oncall notifications.

Signal catalog (priority ordering)
1) Safety/Hard-fail signals: 5xxs from the runtime, timeouts > configured SLO, degradation of model availability. Action: immediate automatic rollback.
2) Latency & throughput: median/95/99 latencies per route, tokens/sec. Thermal trigger: if p99 > baseline + 200ms for > 5m, escalate to steward.
3) Cost telemetry: tokens per response and per-request CPU/GPU-ms. If cost per fulfilled request increases > 25% relative to baseline for two consecutive windows (10m), flag for review.
4) Quality probes: semantic correctness on 100 golden prompts per stage and 300 sampling prompts for high-volume slices. Failure threshold: BLEU/ROUGE-like metric drop or manual score drop > 6 points.
5) Behavioral drift: change in entity-extraction precision/recall, hallucination rate. If hallucination rate increases by absolute 2% on a prioritized slice, hold.
6) User-impact metrics: funnel conversion, search click-through rate. Use rolling 24h baseline for comparison.

Safety and escape hatches (fast paths)
- Immediate rollback conditions (auto): runtime 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes; model unavailable; infra pressure OOMs on serving nodes.
- Steward immediate manual rollback: major quality regression on golden prompts (team consensus), or user-impact KPI degradation > 3% in a sensitive funnel.
- Soft-fallback: route failing cohorts to fallback model variant (quantized or prior checkpoint) while keeping the rest live. Ensure fallback route is warmed before activation.

Experiment design notes (A/B within canary)
- Use layered assignment: simultaneously run A/B within the canary slice at stage B to test a small model change (eg. prompt tweak or safety filter) against the main candidate. Keep the overall canary traffic budget same.
- Experiment keys: use deterministic hashing by user id when possible to avoid contamination across stages. Log assignment in request metadata for traceability.

Data collection checklist (pre-flight)
- Confirm data pipelines exporting: request ids, model id/version, tokens in/out, per-request latency, route id, user cohort tag.
- Golden prompt harness: new run passes smoke check (>=95% previously expected labels).
- Synthetic probes: 200 synthetic requests per slice queued to warm caches and exercise edge sequences.
- Tracing: distributed trace contains model runtime name and kernel variant.
- Alerts: pager triggers defined for all auto-rollback signals and cross-team watchers added.

Human review ritual (30–45 minutes)
- Quick readout of top deltas (latency, cost, top failing prompts).
- Sample review: 20 hand-selected examples from failure bucket and 20 random examples from high-volume slice. Use zoom-in template: prompt, expected behavior, actual output, severity, suggested action.
- Decision rubric: proceed if no auto-rollback signal AND human severity-average <= 1.5 (scale 0–3) AND cost delta acceptable to finance owner.

Operational knobs to tune during sprint
- Exposure cadence: shorten windows if early signals show strong stability (e.g., move from 48h observation to 12h).
- Batch sizes and concurrency: watch for throughput cliffs when increasing batch depth.
- Prefix caching ratio: enable progressive prefix caching for stable prompts only; disable for exploratory slices.

Common failure modes & mitigations observed in past lab runs
- Latency cliff at 5% due to garbage collection on a particular CUDA kernel: mitigation -> pin kernel variant and re-profile.
- Price-per-token spike driven by unexpected context length growth: mitigation -> add request length cap and monitor distribution.
- A/B contamination due to sticky cookie assignment across reroutes: mitigation -> rework assignment to include model-version tag in sticky logic.

Post-sprint artifacts to produce (short)
- 1-page decision log: timeline of stage starts, hold/advance decisions, key signals and final disposition.
- Ops runbook updates: add any new auto-rollback triggers uncovered.
- Short learning memo: 3 bullets on what changed in telemetry, 3 action items.

Notes to self / messy checklist (for on-the-ground running)
- Bring printed list of 10 golden prompts to review offline.
- Slack channel: #canary-lab-sprint (post stage start and decision results).
- Backup stewards: list pager sequence.
- Keep a 1-page rollback command cheat-sheet in a pinned comment.

Open questions for sprint kickoff
- Which exact slices are in scope for Stage B expansion? (search rerank, checkout message, in-product help).
- Finance owner: who will sign cost deltas for >15% during canary window?
- Do we want to gate by both cost and quality jointly, or allow quality wins if cost increases slightly? (propose: allow up to 10% cost increase if quality delta >= 4 points, requires signoff).

Immediate next steps (before Day 0)
- Telemetry observer to publish signal dashboards (template: canary-lab-sprint template).
- Ops to verify fallback model warmed and smoke passed.
- Steward to assign human reviewers and schedule cadence blocks on calendar.

End of notebook entry — keep this as the sprint runbook for the next micro-canary. Update this doc with the decision log and tagged links to the postmortem at the end.
